sections.skill: Prove that vertical angles are congruent

questions.skill: Prove that vertical angles are congruent
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Angles 1 and 2 form a linear pair. Angles 2 and 3 form a linear pair. Explain why angle 1 and angle 3 have the same measure.
questions.prompt_markup:
Angles 1 and 2 form a linear pair. Angles 2 and 3 form a linear pair.
Explain why angle 1 and angle 3 have the same measure.
questions.correct_answer: Each one equals 180° minus the measure of angle 2.

questions.skill: Prove that vertical angles are congruent
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Two lines intersect, forming angles 1, 2, 3, and 4 in order around the point. Prove that angle 2 = angle 4. Give a reason for each step.
questions.prompt_markup: Two lines intersect, forming angles 1, 2, 3, and 4 in order around the point. Prove that angle 2 = angle 4. Give a reason for each step.
questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Example: angle 1 + angle 2 = 180° and angle 1 + angle 4 = 180° (linear pairs); so angle 2 = 180° - angle 1 = angle 4 (subtraction property of equality). Other valid chains are accepted. The conclusion without reasons is not full credit.

questions.skill: Prove that vertical angles are congruent
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A proof that vertical angles are congruent says: Step 1: angle 1 + angle 2 = 180° Step 2: angle 2 + angle 3 = 180° Step 3: angle 1 + angle 2 = angle 2 + angle 3 Step 4: angle 1 = angle 3 What is the reason for Step 4?
questions.prompt_markup:
A proof that vertical angles are congruent says:
Step 1: angle 1 + angle 2 = 180°
Step 2: angle 2 + angle 3 = 180°
Step 3: angle 1 + angle 2 = angle 2 + angle 3
Step 4: angle 1 = angle 3
What is the reason for Step 4?

questions.skill: Prove that vertical angles are congruent
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Two lines intersect, and one of the four angles is 90°. Prove that all four angles are 90°.
questions.prompt_markup:
Two lines intersect, and one of the four angles is 90°.
Prove that all four angles are 90°.
questions.correct_answer: Each angle next to the 90° angle forms a linear pair with it, so it measures 180° - 90° = 90°. The angle opposite the 90° angle is vertical to it, so it also measures 90°.
questions.grading_note: Full credit needs a reason for each angle (linear pairs and vertical angles).

questions.skill: Prove that vertical angles are congruent
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: "Angles 1 and 3 are vertical angles, and they look equal, so angle 1 = angle 3" is a valid proof.
questions.prompt_markup: "Angles 1 and 3 are vertical angles, and they look equal, so angle 1 = angle 3" is a valid proof.
questions.grading_note: A proof needs reasons such as linear pairs, not how the angles look.
